_nota: Inglés de la PROSA del Paso 2. El vocabulario AO y el derivado de clasificaciones regionales los genera tools/traducir_paso2.py; el generador funde ambas fuentes. Aquí solo va lo redactado a mano.
preguntaClave: What exactly is this fracture, and what does that label anticipate about the rest of the plan?
sintesis: The label contains the indication. Classify with AO/OTA (bone-segment-type) on good radiographs, lean on the regional satellite, refine with CT in articular and periarticular fractures — it complements, it is not a requirement — and read in the label the conduct that will guide Steps 3 to 10. With Steps 1 and 2 done properly, half the operation has already been thought through.
objetivos: Build the AO/OTA code from bone, segment and type
Read the letter A/B/C in its context: it means different things in the shaft, in an articular segment and in the malleoli
Choose the satellite classification that adds what AO/OTA does not capture in that region
Recognise when CT refines the classification, knowing that it is not a requirement for classifying
Accept non-operative treatment and primary arthroplasty as legitimate outcomes of the method

esencial.texto: Classifying is the second act of planning, not an academic formality. A good classification is a treatment hypothesis: when we say «complete multifragmentary articular fracture» we have already said, implicitly, «I will need anatomical reduction, absolute stability of the surface and, probably, bridging of the metaphysis».
The label contains the indication. If the classification does not suggest a course of action, either it has not been classified properly or information is missing.

items: Bone (1st digit): 1 humerus · 2 ulna and radius · 3 femur · 4 tibia and fibula. Hand, foot, pelvis and spine have their own.
Segment (2nd digit): 1 proximal · 2 diaphyseal · 3 distal. Tibia and fibula add 4 for the malleoli.
Type (A/B/C): the layer that carries most prognostic weight; it means different things in the shaft and in an articular segment.
Group and subgroup (1, 2, 3 and .1–.3): they detail the morphology and refine the severity within the type.
Universal qualifiers: the AO/OTA-2018 revision added common qualifiers (articular involvement, fragmentation, location) that standardise the nuances between bones.

filas: Simple: a single line (spiral, oblique or transverse). Two fragments.
Wedge: a third fragment; after reduction, contact between the main fragments persists.
Compression or bridging, depending on the wedge.
Complex or multifragmentary: no reconstructable contact between the main fragments.

esencial.titulo: Articular segment — what the letter means
filas: Extra-articular: the line does not enter the surface.
Partial articular: part of the surface remains attached to the shaft.
Rebuild the surface; often a buttress.
Complete articular: the surface is entirely separated from the shaft.
Anatomical and absolute at the surface; metaphyseal bridging.

esencial.titulo: The same letter says opposite things
esencial.texto: A diaphyseal B is a wedge; an articular B is a partial fracture of the surface; a malleolar B is a fibular line at the level of the syndesmosis; a pelvic ring B is rotational instability. Always read the letter in its context.

esencial.titulo: Satellite classifications — the trunk is the AO/OTA
filas: Displacement, block, comminution; ORIF versus replacement.
Displacement and verticality of the line; risk of necrosis.
Pattern of depression and split; approach and support.
Level of the fibula and mechanism; syndesmotic stability.
Stability and location; risk of non-union.
Mechanism and stability of the ring.

items: Inter- and intraobserver variability: agreement is good for the type (A/B/C) and falls in the fine subgroups. Useful for strategy, not for millimetre distinctions.
Believing you cannot classify without CT: the radiograph classifies; CT refines. In articular and periarticular fractures it is worth complementing, but it is not a requirement.
Classifying on a poor image: inadequate or badly centred projections lead to error. Insist on the right ones, and on the contralateral side when it helps.
Classifying without assessing the patient: the biggest trap. A perfect bony label on a badly assessed host leads to failure. Always go back to Step 1.

esencial.titulo: Not operating is also a decision of the method
esencial.texto: The book is about solving any fracture, not about operating on any fracture. Many fractures — a large share of proximal and shaft humerus, clavicle, ribs, stable pelvic ring, undisplaced fractures — heal better with a brace and rehabilitation. The method is worked through just the same: the best stability may be that of a splint and the best approach, none at all.

In certain settings it is not a salvage plan: the displaced subcapital femoral neck fracture in the elderly, or the comminuted, unreconstructable articular fracture of the distal or proximal humerus in very osteoporotic bone. Recognising it in Step 2 avoids internal fixations that were condemned from the start.

alertas.titulo: The biggest trap: classifying without assessing
alertas.texto: A perfect bony label on a badly assessed host or badly assessed soft tissues leads to failure. If you have not completed Step 1, go back before going on.

alertas.titulo: Read the letter in its context
alertas.texto: You are in an articular segment: here A means extra-articular, not «simple».

alertas.titulo: In the shaft, B1 and C1 no longer exist
alertas.texto: The 2018 revision removed the spiral wedge (B1) and the complex spiral (C1). The diaphyseal groups are A1, A2, A3, B2, B3, C2 and C3.

alertas.titulo: In the scapula the letter is the location
alertas.texto: 14A is the process, 14B the body and 14F the glenoid fossa — with F, not with C. The glenoid also has a group 0 (14F0) for the extra-articular neck.
The compendium leaves a gap between dots for the number of the ray, digit, rib or vertebra. Without filling it in, the code is incomplete.

alertas.titulo: Articular: CT refines and frequently reclassifies
alertas.texto: In the plateau, pilon, calcaneus, distal humerus, distal radius and acetabulum, CT often changes the type, reveals key fragments and guides the approach. It is not a requirement for classifying, but without it the injury is underestimated.
In the transsyndesmotic line the syndesmotic injury is variable, and in the suprasyndesmotic one it is constant. Its malreduction is the key complication of the ankle.
Group 31A2 incorporates the lateral wall threshold of ≤ 20.5 mm. With an incompetent lateral wall the DHS fails: the indication is a cephalomedullary nail.

alertas.titulo: Reliability: good for the type, lower for the subgroup
alertas.texto: Interobserver agreement is good for the letter and falls in groups and subgroups. It serves to decide the strategy, not to argue over millimetre distinctions.

evidencia.afirmacion: Interobserver agreement for the AO/OTA is good for the type (A/B/C) and falls in the fine subgroups: useful for strategy, not for millimetre distinctions.
In the plateau, pilon, calcaneus and distal humerus, CT frequently changes the type and reveals key fragments that plain radiographs do not show.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Why is it said that «classifying well is starting to plan»?
opciones: Because it allows the case to be coded for the notes
Because the right label already anticipates stability, reduction, principle, approach and complications
Because it is an administrative requirement before operating
Because it allows series to be compared between hospitals
autoevaluacion.explicacion: If the classification does not suggest a course of action, either the classification or the information is missing. Comparing series is an added benefit, not the clinical reason.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: When is it worth complementing an articular classification with CT?
opciones: Always: without CT you cannot classify
Never: CT belongs to the postoperative work-up
In articular and periarticular fractures, because it refines and frequently reclassifies
Only if the radiograph is poorly taken
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The classification is established with a radiograph. CT adds detail in articular and periarticular fractures — plateau, pilon, calcaneus, distal humerus, distal radius, acetabulum — showing fragments and depressions the radiograph underestimates.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: A fracture coded 42-B. What does the letter B mean here?
opciones: Partial articular fracture of the proximal tibia
Wedge fracture of the tibial shaft
A fibular line at the level of the syndesmosis
Rotational instability of the ring
autoevaluacion.explicacion: 4 = tibia and fibula, 2 = shaft. In the shaft, B is the wedge fracture: there is a third fragment but, after reduction, contact between the main ones persists.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: And in a 41-B, what does the same letter mean?
opciones: Wedge fracture of the metaphysis
Extra-articular fracture of the proximal tibia
Partial articular fracture: part of the surface remains attached to the shaft
Complete articular fracture
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Same bone, different segment, different meaning. In an articular segment, B is the partial articular fracture, which usually demands a buttress principle.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: A complete articular fracture (type C) anticipates which combination in the following steps?
opciones: Relative stability throughout the construct and functional reduction
Anatomical reduction and absolute stability at the surface, with metaphyseal bridging
Pure bridging with an intramedullary nail
Interfragmentary compression of every fragment
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The articular surface demands anatomical and absolute; the comminuted metaphysis is bridged. It is the classic example of combining two principles in one construct.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: In a diaphyseal wedge fracture, what is the commonest error?
opciones: Using a nail instead of a plate
Chasing and stripping the wedge in order to reduce it anatomically
Not requesting CT before operating
Classifying it as type C
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The wedge is reduced if it can be done without devitalising it. Chasing it at the cost of its blood supply turns a mechanical problem into a biological one.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: What is the BIGGEST trap of classification?
opciones: Interobserver variability in the subgroups
Not having CT available
Classifying without having assessed the patient and the soft tissues
Using a satellite classification instead of the AO/OTA
autoevaluacion.explicacion: A perfect bony label on a badly assessed host leads to failure. The classification does not replace Step 1.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: An elderly patient with a displaced subcapital femoral neck fracture. How does the method read it in Step 2?
opciones: As an indication for fixation with cannulated screws
As an indication for primary arthroplasty, not for salvage
As a fracture for non-operative treatment
As a fracture that does not need classifying
autoevaluacion.explicacion: Recognising arthroplasty as primary treatment in Step 2 avoids internal fixations condemned from the start. In the active, independent patient, total hip replacement is the choice.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: What does a satellite classification add that the AO/OTA does not capture?
opciones: It replaces the AO/OTA in that region
It captures regional nuances that change the treatment of that particular bone
It is only useful for publishing series
It allows you to do without CT
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The AO/OTA is the trunk and the satellites orbit around it: Neer adds the vascular prognosis, Letournel-Judet the approach, Weber the syndesmotic stability. They do not compete: they complement.

autoevaluacion.pregunta: Non-operative treatment of a humeral shaft fracture. Which statement is correct?
opciones: It means the method does not apply to this case
It is the failure of the method in the face of an unsolvable fracture
It is a legitimate outcome of the method: the same steps are worked through
It is only accepted if the patient refuses surgery
autoevaluacion.explicacion: The method is about solving, not about operating. The best stability may be that of a brace and the best approach, none at all. What does not change is the duty to define follow-up and the threshold for conversion.
